advances: A sharp one-dimensional ordinary marginal comparison, including its positive-simplex-normal specialization.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The marginal is nonatomic, since level sets are hyperplanes, and its support is $[0,b]$. Both cap-volume roots $F^{1/d}$ and $(1-F)^{1/d}$ are concave on this interval. For either choice of cap direction, the Minkowski interpolation of two nonempty caps is contained in the cap at the interpolated threshold, so ordinary Brunn–Minkowski gives the concavity, including the zero-volume end cap.

Fix $0<t<b$. Write $\alpha=F(t)\in(0,1)$ and $q=(1-\alpha)^{1/d}$. The lower root chord from $0$ to $t$ yields $F(s)\ge\alpha(s/t)^d$ for $0\le s\le t$. The upper root has value one at zero and value $q$ at $t$. Its secant slopes give $(1-F(s))^{1/d}\le1-(1-q)s/t$ for $t\le s\le b$. At $s=b$ this implies $b\le t/(1-q)$, so the affine upper bound is nonnegative on the needed interval. Beyond $b$ the tail is zero. Integrate the lower-root consequence on $[0,t]$ and the positive part of the affine upper bound to the power $d$ on $[t,\infty)$:
$$
\frac{\mu}{t}\le 1-\frac{\alpha}{d+1}
   +\frac{q^{d+1}}{(d+1)(1-q)}
   =\frac{d+q^d/(1-q)}{d+1}.
$$
Multiplying the numerator on the right by $\alpha$ gives $d(1-q^d)+q^d(1+q+\cdots+q^{d-1})\le d$, strictly if $d\ge2$. At $t=0$ the inequality holds since $F(0)=0$. For $t\ge b$ use the chord $F(s)\ge(s/b)^d$ on $[0,b]$, which gives $\mu\le db/(d+1)\le dt/(d+1)$. Nonatomicity and nonnegativity of the tail then give the closed-tail comparison.

A cone with its apex at height zero and base at height $b$ has $F(s)=(s/b)^d$ for $s\in[0,b]$. Its mean is $db/(d+1)$, attaining the coefficient at $t=b$; increasing the length of the comparison uniform interval would give positive tail at $b$ for that uniform law. Reflecting this example in the height interval gives $F(s)=1-(1-s/b)^d$ and mean $b/(d+1)$, so $\mu F(t)/t$ tends to the same sharp coefficient as $t\downarrow0$. In dimension one the marginal is uniform and equality holds for $0\le t\le b$.

For the specified simplex marginal the minimum is zero, the mean is $r/(d+1)$, and the full volume is $|T_d|r^d$. Multiplying the tail estimate by that volume proves the last assertion. The comparison corresponds to uniform mass $|T_d|r^d$ on $[0,r/d]$. At the simplex centroid threshold it pays only a $1/(d+1)$ fraction, below $(d/(d+1))^d$ for $d\ge2$.
statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body, $d\ge1$, and $Y$ a nonconstant affine functional of its uniform point with minimum zero on $K$. Write $b=\max_KY$, $\mu=\mathbb EY$, and $F(t)=\Pr(Y\le t)$. Then
$$
\mu F(t)\le\frac{dt}{d+1},
\qquad
\Pr(Y\ge t)\ge\left[1-\frac{dt}{(d+1)\mu}\right]_+\qquad(t\ge0).
$$
The coefficient $d/(d+1)$ and the corresponding dominated uniform interval length $(d+1)\mu/d$ are sharp. For $d\ge2$ the first inequality is strict for $0<t<b$. In particular, for $r>0$, the standard $d$-simplex $T_d=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, and $w_i\ge0$ with $\sum_iw_i=1$,
$|rT_d\cap\{x:w\cdot x\ge t\}|\ge |T_d|r^d[1-dt/r]_+$ for $t\ge0$.
title: Sharp uniform comparison for a nonnegative convex-body marginal
